title: Why You See Colours Differently After Staring At Another Colour
hook: Your eyes can actually see colours that are not there.

narration.text: Your eyes can actually see colours that are not there.
This happens due to something called opponent process theory.
Your cone cells in the eye process colours in opposing pairs.
These pairs are red versus green, blue versus yellow, and black versus white.
When you stare at one colour, like red, those cells become fatigued.
Look away and the opposing colour, green, overcompensates.
This creates a vivid afterimage in the opposite colour.
It is why you see a green flash after staring at a red object.
Have you ever noticed this surprising effect yourself?

description: Ever wondered why you sometimes see colours differently after staring at another colour? It is all down to opponent process theory and how your eyes process light. This short video explains the fascinating science behind these visual afterimages.
topic: Why you sometimes see colours differently after staring at another colour, explaining opponent process theory.
